subject.title: Gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages

question: Which restart-recovery architecture should own this issue: a SQLite-backed durable followup queue, the SIGUSR1 drain mitigation, or a successor design that combines durable followups with channel-level replay?
rationale: The issue is valid, but the fix spans core gateway shutdown, process-local followup queues, durable state, and channel acknowledgment contracts; automation should not choose between the existing open designs.

options.title: Advance a SQLite-backed successor
options.body: Use a shared-state SQLite-backed queue as the canonical design, require upgrade-safe storage and live channel proof, and fold in drain-window replay semantics before closing this issue.

options.title: Split the phases
options.body: Land a narrow followup persistence or SIGUSR1 drain fix first, then leave downtime catch-up and channel ACK deferral to broader restart-recovery issues.

options.title: Pause current branches
options.body: Close or pause the broad candidate PRs if maintainers want a redesigned core/plugin API before durable replay work lands.

recommendation.title: Advance a SQLite-backed successor
recommendation.body: Use a shared-state SQLite-backed queue as the canonical design, require upgrade-safe storage and live channel proof, and fold in drain-window replay semantics before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged restart-drain work is the strongest code-history routing signal for this architecture choice.
